claims.text: HEA nanoparticles containing five or more metals in equal or near-equal ratios can initially form a homogeneous solid-solution phase.
Atomic-size differences among the constituent elements produce measurable lattice distortion.
The initial nanoparticles exhibit minimal short-range chemical ordering.
High configurational entropy favors formation and preservation of a single solid-solution phase over intermetallic formation or phase segregation.
Lattice distortion lowers atomic diffusivity in HEAs.
Reduced atomic diffusion caused by lattice distortion inhibits phase segregation at elevated temperatures.
At elevated temperature, configurational entropy lowers the free energy of the disordered solid-solution phase.
Pronounced lattice distortions create energy barriers to atomic migration.
Configurational-entropy stabilization and distortion-limited migration act synergistically to preserve structural and chemical homogeneity during thermal stress.
Nanoparticles having high configurational entropy and pronounced lattice distortion will remain single-phase and chemically uniform after prolonged exposure throughout 473–1923 K.
Reduced-distortion nanoparticles will exhibit more elemental segregation and phase transformation than high-distortion nanoparticles under identical thermal conditions.
Substantial atomic-size mismatch is required to obtain the lattice distortion relevant to the predicted stability.
The stability prediction depends on synthesis producing a randomly mixed solid solution.
Using an inert or otherwise controlled atmosphere minimizes oxidation or other external chemical effects, allowing intrinsic HEA stability to be assessed.
Nanoscale surface segregation could alter the thermal response relative to expectations based on bulk HEAs.
New X-ray diffraction peaks or peak splitting can indicate new-phase formation or phase separation.
High-resolution elemental mapping can assess chemical homogeneity in the nanoparticles.
Changes in catalytic or thermoelectric performance can serve as a proxy for structural integrity.
Similar phase separation, chemical inhomogeneity, or performance degradation in the high- and low-distortion groups would falsify the predicted stabilizing role of lattice distortion.
